questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road has low clearance.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for any traffic you might have missed.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Wait until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a DUII for the first time, how long is your license suspended?

options.text: Six months
Three months
One year
Two years

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: A first DUII conviction results in a one-year license suspension.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your wheel into traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your vehicle skids. Steer in the direction the back of your vehicle is sliding.

questions.question: Your stopping ability is affected by:

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition is the main factor that affects your stopping ability. Slow down on slippery or poor roads to keep control of your vehicle and have time to stop.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph needs up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need much longer to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: When you drive faster:

options.text: Your field of vision gets wider.
Your field of vision gets narrower.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
Your field of vision does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your field of vision gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision decreases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what is your first step?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: Stop parallel to the vehicle in front of your desired parking space. Check traffic and signal first. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: By driving a vehicle in Oregon, you agree to:

options.text: Keep liability insurance for as long as you drive.
Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
Post bail or go to court if arrested for a traffic violation.
Keep your vehicle's equipment in good working condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
questions.explanation: Oregon's Implied Consent Law says that by driving, you agree to take a breath, blood, or urine test if a police officer asks after arresting you for driving under the influence. Refusing this test has serious legal consequences.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign (with the arrow) shows where bicycles cross or ride beside traffic. Drive carefully in this area.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Make your vehicle need a tune-up sooner than usual.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start fires in grass on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system can cause death very quickly. They can also make you feel sleepy while driving.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to travel on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road when conditions are ideal. You may drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones or work zones. If weather, construction, or other conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one train passes. Do not cross the tracks until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection—controlled or uncontrolled—when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this hand signal.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. You may:

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never cross these lines.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road has a sharp curve in the direction the chevron points. In this case, the road curves to the left. You may see several chevron signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: When facing a car with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has its high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should adjust when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First, adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.
